newsitem.title: UK: Windfall tax challenge could not succeed - UK Labour.
newsitem.headline: Windfall tax challenge could not succeed - UK Labour.

text.p: There is no chance of a legal challenge to the opposition Labour Party's planned windfall tax on privatised utilities succeeding, shadow chief secretary to the Treasury Alistair Darling said on Sunday.
"We are satisfied that there is no possibility of a successful challenge either under European law or under domestic law," he told BBC radio.
Darling was commenting on a claim from the right-wing pressure group Aims of Industry that the tax on electricity, gas and water companies would be against European Union law.
"I think people should understand that the windfall tax is not up for negotiation, it is not up for grabs," he said.
"I think that what we are seeing here is some political manoeuvring. We have seen it over the last few months and I dare say it will continue up to the election.
"We are not going to be deflected by this sort of speculation whether it comes from lawyers or anybody else," he added.
The tax is a key Labour pledge in the run-up to the general election. Labour plans to levy it to help the young and long-term unemployed into work.
